records.source: Παῦλος δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, κλητὸς ἀπόστολος, ἀφωρισμένος εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ ὃ προεπηγγείλατο διὰ τῶν προφητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν γραφαῖς ἁγίαις περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα, τοῦ ὁρισθέντος υἱοῦ θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, δι’ οὗ ἐλάβομεν χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἀγαπητοῖς θεοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: Paul, slave of Christ Jesus, called apostle, having been set apart for gospel of God, \v 2 which he promised beforehand through the prophets of him in writings holy \v 3 concerning the Son of him, the [one] having come from seed of David according to flesh, \v 4 the [one] having been appointed Son of God in power according to spirit of holiness from resurrection of dead [ones], Jesus Christ the Lord of us, \v 5 through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations on behalf of the name of him, \v 6 among whom are also you called of Jesus Christ, \v 7 to all the [ones] being in Rome beloved of God, called holy [ones]; grace to you and peace from God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ.
pieces: From Paul, a servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, called to be an apostle and set apart for the gospel of God.
God promised this gospel long ago through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets in the holy Scriptures.
It concerns {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, who by human descent was born of the line of David,
and who was appointed Son of God in power, through the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection of the dead: Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} our Lord.
Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have received grace and apostleship, to bring about the obedience of faith among all the nations for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
You are among them, you whom Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has called to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own.
To all of you in Rome whom God loves and has called to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people: grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.1: Paul, a slave of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, called [to be] an apostle, set apart for [the] gospel of God,
L.2: which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised beforehand through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets in [the] holy Scriptures,
L.3: concerning {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, who came from [the] seed of David according to [the] flesh,
L.4: who was appointed Son of God in power according to [the] Spirit of holiness from [the] resurrection of [the] dead, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} our Lord,
L.5: through whom we received grace and apostleship for [the] obedience of faith among all the nations on behalf of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name,
L.6: among whom are you also, called [to belong] to Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.7: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called [to be] holy ones: grace to you and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.1: This letter is from Paul. I am a servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. God called me to be an apostle and chose me to tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} good news.
R.2: Long ago God promised this good news through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets, and their promises are written in the holy Scriptures.
R.3: The good news is about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. As a human being, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was born into the family line of King David.
R.4: Through the Holy Spirit, God appointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be the Son of God with power when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead. He is Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, our Lord.
R.5: Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, God has given us grace and sent us out as apostles. We are sent to people of all the nations, so that they will come to faith and obey God. We do this for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
R.6: You are among those people too. Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has called you to belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.7: So I am writing to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has called you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people. May God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} give you grace and peace.

decisions.reason: δοῦλος is a slave, a person owned by another. Paul calls himself the slave of Christ Jesus: he belongs to him entirely and acts at his command. The word also recalls the Old Testament title "servant of the LORD" given to Moses, David and the prophets, so it is a title of honor as well as of belonging.

ὁρίζω means to mark out, set or appoint (Acts 10:42 and 17:31 use it of Jesus appointed judge). Verse 3 already calls him God's Son, so the point is not that he became Son at the resurrection, but that by it he was installed as Son of God "in power": the risen Son now reigning. "Declared" is a common alternative, but the word is stronger than an announcement.

The phrase stands next to "Son of God" and contrasts with verse 3: born of David's line in weakness ("according to the flesh"), appointed Son of God in power. Read with the verb, it would only say how the appointing was done.

alternatives: Christ's own holy spirit or nature, set against his human nature ("flesh") in verse 3
decisions.reason: "Spirit of holiness" is a Hebrew way of saying "Holy Spirit" (Psalm 51:13 and Isaiah 63:10-11 have the same phrase in Hebrew). Verses 3-4 set "according to the flesh" against "according to the Spirit", as Paul does elsewhere (8:4-5, Galatians 4:29), and for Paul the Spirit is the one who raised Jesus (8:11). Some read it of Christ's own spirit, the holy nature that was his alongside his human descent. The levels follow the first reading.

decisions.choice: by the resurrection of the dead
decisions.reason: ἐξ can give the means ("by") or the starting point ("from the time of"); both make the resurrection the moment of the appointing. "The resurrection of the dead" is plural: Jesus' rising is the first of the resurrection God promised to the dead, not only his own return to life (1 Corinthians 15:20).

decisions.choice: "we" means Paul, possibly with the other apostles
decisions.reason: Romans is from Paul alone (1:1), and in verses 8-16 he says "I". The plural here is most likely his own grace and apostleship in a modest form, though it may include the other apostles. The translation keeps "we".

decisions.choice: grace and apostleship: the grace of being an apostle
alternatives: two separate gifts: grace (for salvation) and apostleship
decisions.reason: Paul often speaks of his calling as a grace given to him (12:3, 15:15-16), so the two words most likely name one gift. The levels keep both words and leave the relation open.

decisions.choice: the obedience that consists in faith and flows from it
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and can be read several ways. Paul uses "obey" of believing the gospel (10:16) and also expects faith to issue in obedience (6:16-17). The phrase most likely holds both. The phrase comes again at 16:26.

ἔθνος means nations or peoples, and in Jewish use the nations other than Israel, the Gentiles. Paul was sent especially to the Gentiles (11:13, 15:16), and his readers in Rome are among them (verse 6). "All the nations" keeps the scope of his mission; verse 13 has the same word where the sense "Gentiles" is clearer.

decisions.choice: called to belong to Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: In Paul it is God who calls (8:30, 9:24), so "of Jesus Christ" says to whom they belong, not who called them.

decisions.choice: called to be holy ones, God's people
decisions.reason: ἅγιος is "holy", here as a noun: people set apart for God. It is what all believers are, not a few outstanding ones, as the Old Testament called Israel a holy people (Exodus 19:6).

alternatives: a few manuscripts leave out "in Rome" here and in verse 15
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts have "in Rome" in verses 7 and 15. A few, among them a Greek-Latin manuscript of the ninth century, leave it out, perhaps from copies made for general reading in the churches. The SBLGNT keeps it. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

Letters of the time opened with "From A to B, greetings". Paul fills the greeting with grace and peace, the gift of God and the wholeness that follows from it (in Hebrew, shalom). His greeting here is the longest of his letters, because he has not yet visited Rome and introduces himself and his gospel.
Title setting.

decisions.choice: the greeting opens "From Paul" and ends its first sentence at verse 1
alternatives: one sentence to the end of verse 7
decisions.reason: The Greek greeting runs from verse 1 to verse 7 as one sentence. Balanced breaks it after each step of Paul's description so a listener can follow it, and opens with "From" so the first sentence reads as the sender of a letter, as Philippians 1:1 does.

decisions.choice: King David; for the honor of his name
decisions.reason: Readable adds "King" so a new reader knows who David is. "His name" is Jesus Christ's, who is named just before.
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: Πρῶτον μὲν εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καταγγέλλεται ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.
records.gloss: First indeed I thank the God of me through Jesus Christ concerning all of you, because the faith of you is being proclaimed in whole the world.
pieces: To begin with, I thank my God through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} for every one of you, because people throughout the whole world are speaking of your faith.

L.8: First, I thank my God through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed in the whole world.

R.8: First, I thank my God through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} for all of you. People all over the world are hearing about your faith.

decisions.reason: Πρῶτον μὲν usually begins a list, but Paul never reaches a "second". It means "to begin with": the first thing he does is give thanks.

decisions.choice: Paul's thanks reach God through Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Paul gives thanks through Jesus Christ, as he says all access to God comes through him (5:2, 7:25).
"In the whole world" is a natural way of saying "everywhere": the church in the capital was known among believers across the Roman world (16:19 says the same).
Title setting.

decisions.choice: people ... are speaking of / are hearing about your faith
decisions.reason: The passive "is being proclaimed" leaves out who proclaims it. Balanced and Readable name them as people, which is what the passive means.

records.heading: Paul longs to visit Rome

records.source: μάρτυς γάρ μού ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, δεόμενος εἴ πως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
records.gloss: Witness for of me is the God, whom I serve in the spirit of me in the gospel of the Son of him, how unceasingly mention of you I make \v 10 always at the prayers of me, asking if somehow now at last I will be prospered in the will of the God to come to you.
pieces: God, whom I serve with my whole spirit in proclaiming the gospel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, can testify how constantly I remember you
in my prayers. I am always asking that somehow, if God wills it, the way may at last be opened for me to come to you.

L.9: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you,
L.10: always at my prayers asking if somehow now at last I may be given a good way, by the will of God, to come to you.

R.9: God knows that I am telling the truth. I serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all my heart by telling the good news about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. And God knows that I never stop praying for you.
R.10: Every time I pray, I ask God to make a way for me to come and visit you at last, if that is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

decisions.choice: an oath: God can confirm that this is true
decisions.reason: "God is my witness" calls on God to confirm what Paul says, as people swore by God in court. Paul uses it where readers who have not met him might doubt his words (2 Corinthians 1:23, Philippians 1:8).
λατρεύω is the word for serving God in worship, used of priests in the temple. Paul's preaching of the gospel is his worship (15:16 calls it priestly service).

decisions.choice: with my spirit: inwardly, with all of himself
decisions.reason: "My spirit" is Paul's own inner life, the opposite of outward ritual (as in 2:29). His service is whole-hearted and sincere, not only outward.

decisions.choice: be given a good way, succeed
decisions.reason: εὐοδόομαι once meant to have a good journey, but in Paul's time it meant to succeed or be helped along. Here the two meet: he prays for the way to Rome to open.

decisions.choice: God knows that I am telling the truth; with all my heart
alternatives: God is my witness; in my spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what the oath and "in my spirit" mean instead of reproducing them, since both are unfamiliar idioms.

records.source: ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς, τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν συμπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ.
records.gloss: I long for to see you, that some I may share gift with you spiritual for the to be strengthened you, \v 12 this and is to be encouraged together among you through the in one another faith of you both and of me.
pieces: I long to see you so that I can share some spiritual gift with you that will make you strong.
What I mean is that, while I am with you, we will be encouraged together by each other's faith, yours and mine.

L.11: For I long to see you, so that I may share some spiritual gift with you, so that you may be strengthened,
L.12: that is, so that we may be encouraged together among you through each other's faith, both yours and mine.

R.11: I really want to see you. I want to give you some gift from the Spirit that will help you stand strong.
R.12: What I mean is that we can help each other. Your faith will encourage me, and my faith will encourage you.

decisions.choice: a gift that comes from the Spirit
alternatives: a particular gift such as teaching
decisions.reason: χάρισμα is a gift of grace. With "spiritual" it is a gift the Spirit gives for building others up, as in 12:6 and 1 Corinthians 12. Paul does not say which gift he has in mind.
The verb is passive. Paul gives the gift, but the strength is God's work (16:25 says God is able to strengthen them).

decisions.choice: Paul clarifies: the help goes both ways
decisions.reason: "That is" restates what he has just said. Writing to a church he did not found, he adds at once that he will receive from them as much as he gives.

decisions.choice: a gift from the Spirit; Your faith will encourage me, and my faith will encourage you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "spiritual" means here and spells out "each other's faith" in two plain clauses.

records.source: οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν.
records.gloss: Not I want and you to be unaware, brothers, that many times I purposed to come to you, and was prevented until the present, that some fruit I might have also among you as also among the other nations.
pieces: I want you to know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that I have often planned to come to you, so that I might gather some harvest among you too, as I have among the other Gentiles, but until now I have been kept from coming.

L.13: Now I do not want you to be unaware, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that many times I planned to come to you, and was prevented until now, so that I might have some fruit among you also, just as also among the rest of the Gentiles.

R.13: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I want you to know that many times I have planned to visit you. But each time, something has kept me from coming. I want to see my work bear fruit among you, as it has among other non-Jewish people.

decisions.reason: "I do not want you to be unaware" is Paul's way of introducing something important (11:25, 1 Corinthians 10:1). It says the opposite in negative form, and means a firm "I want you to know".

decisions.choice: Paul was prevented; he does not say by whom
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the cause unnamed. In 15:22 he explains that his work in the eastern provinces kept him from coming.

decisions.choice: fruit: the results of his work
decisions.reason: The fruit is what Paul's ministry produces: people coming to faith and growing in it, as in Philippians 1:22.
The same word as "nations" in verse 5. With "the rest" it means the other non-Jewish peoples Paul has worked among, and it shows that he counts the believers in Rome among the Gentiles.
Paul writes to the whole church, women and men (16:1-15 greets many women by name). "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: the parenthesis "and was prevented until now" moves to the end
decisions.reason: In the Greek the clause about being prevented interrupts the sentence. Balanced moves it to the end so the purpose clause follows the plan it belongs to.
"Gentiles" is church language; Readable says what it means.

records.source: Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί·
records.gloss: To Greeks both and to barbarians, to wise both and to foolish debtor I am;
pieces: I am under obligation to Greeks and to non-Greeks, to the educated and to the uneducated.

L.14: Both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to [the] wise and to [the] foolish, I am a debtor;

R.14: I have a duty to everyone: to people who speak Greek and to those who do not, to the educated and to the uneducated.

decisions.reason: Greek speakers called everyone who did not speak Greek "barbarians", from the sound of a foreign language. The word meant foreigners, not savages. With "Greeks" it covers every people in the empire and beyond it, such as the Spain Paul hopes to reach (15:24).

alternatives: the wise and the foolish (in a moral sense)
decisions.reason: The second pair matches the first: cultured, educated people and simple, unlearned ones. It is about education, not about goodness or folly before God.

alternatives: owing them a debt (something taken from them)
decisions.reason: ὀφειλέτης is a debtor. Paul owes the gospel to all these people: he has received it, and God has given him the task of passing it on (1 Corinthians 9:16).
In English "barbarians" means cruel or uncivilized people, which the Greek word did not. Literal keeps "barbarians" to show the form.

decisions.choice: I have a duty to everyone
decisions.reason: Readable names what the two pairs add up to before listing them.

records.source: οὕτως τὸ κατ’ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι.
records.gloss: So the as to me eager [is] also to you the [ones] in Rome to proclaim the gospel.
pieces: So, for my part, I am eager to bring the gospel to you in Rome as well.

L.15: So, as far as it rests with me, [I am] eager to proclaim the gospel to you also who are in Rome.

R.15: That is why I want so much to tell the good news to you in Rome too.

decisions.choice: for my part, I am eager
decisions.reason: The phrase is a noun, "the eagerness as far as concerns me". Paul is ready; whether he comes depends on God (verse 10).

The Romans already believe (verse 8), yet Paul wants to proclaim the gospel to them. For him the gospel is not only the first message but what believers go on living by, and the letter itself sets it out for them.

alternatives: a few manuscripts leave it out
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, a few manuscripts leave out "in Rome". (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: bring the gospel / tell the good news
decisions.reason: The verb is the one formed from the word gospel: to announce good news. "Preach" suggests a sermon, so Balanced says "bring the gospel" and Readable "tell the good news".

records.source: Οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, δύναμις γὰρ θεοῦ ἐστιν εἰς σωτηρίαν παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·
records.gloss: Not for I am ashamed of the gospel, power for of God it is for salvation to everyone the believing, to Jew both first and to Greek;
pieces: I am not ashamed of the gospel. It is God's own power at work to save everyone who believes, the Jew first and the Greek as well.

L.16: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, both to [the] Jew first and to [the] Greek;

R.16: I am not ashamed of the good news. It is God's power to save everyone who believes. It is for the Jews first, and also for people who are not Jews.

decisions.choice: not ashamed: confident in it, ready to stand by it
decisions.reason: A message about a crucified man was foolishness to many (1 Corinthians 1:23). "Not ashamed" says, by denying the opposite, that Paul stands openly by it, as Jesus speaks of being ashamed of him and his words (Mark 8:38).
The gospel does not only describe God's power: when it is proclaimed and believed, God's power is at work in it to save (1 Corinthians 1:18).

decisions.choice: Greek: anyone who is not a Jew
decisions.reason: Paired with "Jew", "Greek" stands for all non-Jews, Romans included, as in 2:9-10 and 10:12.

decisions.choice: first: Israel's priority in God's plan
decisions.reason: The gospel came first to the Jews, to whom the promises were given (verse 2, 3:2, 9:4-5), and Paul's own mission began in the synagogues. "First" keeps that order, while "everyone who believes" makes the gospel equally for both.
Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb, which English uses more naturally; "save" is one of the key term's settled words.
Readable says what "Greek" means here.

records.heading: The power of the gospel

records.source: δικαιοσύνη γὰρ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται.
records.gloss: Righteousness for of God in it is revealed from faith to faith, as it has been written: The and righteous from faith will live.
pieces: In it the righteousness of God is being revealed, from faith for faith. As it is written, "The one who is righteous will live by faith."

L.17: For in it [the] righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, just as it is written: "But the righteous [one] will live by faith."

R.17: The good news shows God's righteousness: how God puts people right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. It comes by faith, and it leads to faith. As Scripture says, "The person who is righteous will live by faith."

decisions.choice: God's righteousness: God acting rightly to put people right with himself
alternatives: a righteousness that God gives to people (a status from God)
God's own justice or faithfulness, as a quality of God
decisions.reason: In the Psalms and Isaiah, God's righteousness is God acting faithfully to save and set right (Psalm 98:2, Isaiah 46:13, 51:5-8). Romans speaks of it as God's own (3:5, 3:25-26) and also as given to those who believe (3:22, 5:17). The phrase most likely holds both: God shows himself right by putting people right.

decisions.choice: from faith for faith: from start to finish it is by faith
alternatives: from God's faithfulness to human faith
from the faith of one believer to another
from Old Testament faith to New Testament faith
decisions.reason: The phrase gives a starting point and a goal, and both are faith. Paul most likely means that faith is how righteousness is received and where it leads, with nothing else added (as 3:22 says "through faith ... for all who believe"). Other readings take the first "faith" as God's faithfulness.

The quotation is from Habakkuk 2:4. The Hebrew says "the righteous will live by his faithfulness"; most copies of the old Greek translation (the Septuagint) say "by my faithfulness", meaning God's. Paul leaves out the pronoun. He uses the verse again in Galatians 3:11.

alternatives: "by faith" goes with "the righteous": "the one who is righteous by faith will live"
decisions.reason: The Greek order, "the righteous by faith will live", allows both. In Habakkuk the phrase goes with "live", and that reading is followed here. Paul's argument from 1:17 to chapter 5 stresses righteousness by faith and then life (5:1, 5:17-18), so the other reading also fits.

decisions.choice: how God puts people right with himself
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the righteousness of God" as the meaning decision describes it; reviewers should check that it does not narrow the phrase.

decisions.choice: As it is written / As Scripture says
alternatives: just as it has been written
decisions.reason: "It is written" is the normal formula for quoting Scripture; Readable names Scripture.

records.source: Ἀποκαλύπτεται γὰρ ὀργὴ θεοῦ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν ἀδικίᾳ κατεχόντων, διότι τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανερόν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὁ θεὸς γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἐφανέρωσεν.
records.gloss: Is revealed for wrath of God from heaven upon all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people the [ones] the truth in unrighteousness holding down, \v 19 because the known of the God plain is among them, the God for to them made [it] plain.
pieces: God's wrath is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wrongdoing of {{gender:people|men}} who by their wrongdoing hold down the truth.
For what can be known about God is plain to them, because God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has made it plain to them.

L.18: For [the] wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of {{gender:people|men}} who suppress the truth by unrighteousness,
L.19: because what can be known about God is plain among them, for God made [it] plain to them.

R.18: From heaven, God is showing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger against people who do not honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and who do what is wrong. By doing wrong, they push the truth away.
R.19: But they can know the truth about God, because God has made it clear to them.

decisions.choice: God's wrath: his settled opposition to evil and his judgment on it
decisions.reason: ὀργή is anger. God's wrath in Paul is not a fit of temper but his just response to evil, carried out in judgment (2:5-8). The next verses show it at work already: God hands people over to what they have chosen (verses 24, 26, 28).

alternatives: will be revealed at the judgment
decisions.reason: The verb is present, as in verse 17: God's righteousness and his wrath are both being revealed now. Paul also speaks of a coming day of wrath (2:5).

ἀσέβεια is failure to honor God; ἀδικία is wrongdoing, the lack of righteousness. The second word is formed from the same root as "righteousness" in verse 17: God's righteousness is revealed, and so is his wrath against human unrighteousness.
κατέχω can mean to hold fast or to hold back. Here it is to hold the truth down so that it does not act or speak.
"In them" can mean within each person or among people. Verse 20 says God is known through what he made, so the knowledge is open to all, and the translation leaves both open.
Balanced and Readable use plain words for ἀδικία. Literal keeps "unrighteousness" so that the link with "righteousness" in verse 17 stays visible.
"Wrath" is rare in everyday English; Readable says "anger".
The word means human beings, men and women.

records.heading: Humanity turns from the Creator

records.source: τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται, ἥ τε ἀΐδιος αὐτοῦ δύναμις καὶ θειότης, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους, διότι γνόντες τὸν θεὸν οὐχ ὡς θεὸν ἐδόξασαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλὰ ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία·
records.gloss: The for invisible [things] of him from creation of world by the made [things] being understood are clearly seen, the both eternal of him power and divinity, for the to be them without excuse, \v 21 because having known the God not as God they glorified or gave thanks, but they became futile in the reasonings of them and was darkened the senseless of them heart;
pieces: Since the world was made, what cannot be seen of God, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} everlasting power and divine nature, has been in plain view, understood from the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made. So they have no excuse.
Although they knew God, they did not give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory as God or thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Their reasoning turned to emptiness, and darkness filled their senseless hearts.

L.20: For since [the] creation of [the] world {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} invisible [attributes] are clearly seen, being understood through the things made, both {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eternal power and divine nature, so that they are without excuse,
L.21: because, although they knew God, they did not glorify [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] as God or give thanks, but they became futile in their reasonings, and their senseless heart was darkened;

R.20: No one can see God. But since the beginning of the world, people have been able to understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is like from the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made. They can see that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power lasts forever and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is truly God. So people have no excuse.
R.21: They knew God, but they did not give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the glory {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deserves as God, and they did not thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Their thinking became worthless, and their foolish minds were filled with darkness.

decisions.reason: Paul sets the two words side by side on purpose: God, who cannot be seen, is clearly seen by the mind ("being understood") in what he has made.
θειότης is the quality of being divine. Creation shows that its maker is God and has eternal power; it does not show everything about God.

decisions.choice: so that they are without excuse: the result
alternatives: in order that they might be without excuse: God's purpose
decisions.reason: The construction can give purpose or result. The point is the outcome, that no one can plead ignorance, not that God revealed himself in order to condemn.
The participle grants a fact against which the rest stands out: they knew him, yet did not honor him.
ματαιόομαι is to become empty or worthless. The Old Testament calls idols "empty things" and says their makers become like them (Jeremiah 2:5, Psalm 115:8).

decisions.choice: heart: the center of thought and will
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is where a person thinks and decides, not only where they feel. A darkened heart is a mind that no longer sees.
Balanced and Readable use the noun, which is plainer English; the key term allows "glory" for this verb.
In English "heart" suggests feelings; Readable says "minds", as the meaning decision explains.
The word here is not the one Open Word Bible renders "eternal" (as in "eternal life"); "everlasting" keeps them apart.

records.source: φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν, καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.
records.gloss: Claiming to be wise they became foolish, \v 23 and they exchanged the glory of the immortal God in likeness of image of mortal human and of birds and of four-footed [animals] and of creeping [things].
pieces: They claimed to be wise, but they became fools.
They traded the glory of the God who never dies for images made to look like mortal human beings, or birds, or beasts, or creatures that crawl.

L.22: Claiming to be wise, they became fools,
L.23: and they exchanged the glory of the immortal God for a likeness of an image of {{gender:a mortal human|mortal man}} and of birds and of four-footed [animals] and of creeping things.

R.22: They said they were wise, but they became foolish.
R.23: God is glorious and lives forever. But they stopped worshiping {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and worshiped idols instead. They made idols that looked like people, who die, and like birds, animals and creatures that crawl.

decisions.reason: Psalm 106:20 says Israel at the golden calf "exchanged their glory for the image of an ox", and Jeremiah 2:11 says God's people "exchanged their glory" for what does not help. Deuteronomy 4:16-18 forbids images of men or women, animals, birds and creeping things. Paul tells the story of all humanity in Israel's words.
Human beings, birds, four-footed animals and creeping things are the creatures of Genesis 1:20-26. People worshiped the creatures they were made to rule over.

decisions.choice: a likeness of an image: a copy of a copy
decisions.reason: Paul doubles the words: they worshiped not even creatures but a likeness of their image, an idol shaped like them.
ἄφθαρτος is "not subject to decay", φθαρτός "subject to decay": the God who never dies against human beings who die.

decisions.choice: they stopped worshiping him and worshiped idols instead
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "exchanged the glory of God for a likeness of an image" describes: the worship of idols.
The word means a human being. Balanced and Readable already use inclusive words and need no setting.

records.source: Διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς, οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
records.gloss: Therefore handed over them the God in the desires of the hearts of them to impurity of the to be dishonored the bodies of them among them, \v 25 who exchanged the truth of the God in the lie, and worshiped and served the creation beyond the [one] having created, who is blessed into the ages; amen.
pieces: So God handed them over, in the cravings of their hearts, to impurity, and they dishonored their bodies with one another.
They traded the truth about God for the lie. They bowed down to the creation and served it, instead of the one who created it, who is blessed forever. Amen.

L.24: Therefore God handed them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity, so that their bodies were dishonored among them,
L.25: [they] who exchanged the truth of God for the lie and worshiped and served the creation rather than the one who created [it], who is blessed forever. Amen.

R.24: So God handed them over to the impure things their hearts wanted, and they dishonored their bodies with one another.
R.25: They traded the truth about God for a lie. They worshiped and served the things God made, instead of God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, who made them. Praise belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} forever! Amen.

decisions.reason: παραδίδωμι is to hand over, the word for handing a prisoner over to a guard or a judge (Matthew 5:25). Three times (verses 24, 26, 28) God hands people over to what they have chosen: his wrath (verse 18) is at work in letting their choice run its course.

decisions.choice: so that their bodies were dishonored among them
alternatives: to dishonor their bodies among themselves
decisions.reason: The infinitive gives the result. Its form can be passive or middle, "were dishonored" or "dishonored"; either way the dishonor is done among themselves.

decisions.choice: the truth about God for the lie: idolatry
decisions.reason: "The truth of God" is the truth God made known about himself (verses 19-20). "The lie" has the article: the falsehood of idolatry, the lie that something made is God (Jeremiah 13:25, 16:19).
Jews added a blessing when God's name came up, especially after speaking of something that dishonored him. "Amen" (from a Hebrew word meaning firm or true) is the response that confirms it.
The same verb comes three times, and each level repeats the same English so that the pattern stays visible.

decisions.choice: instead of God himself, who made them
decisions.reason: Readable names the Creator as God.

records.source: Διὰ τοῦτο παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς πάθη ἀτιμίας· αἵ τε γὰρ θήλειαι αὐτῶν μετήλλαξαν τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν εἰς τὴν παρὰ φύσιν, ὁμοίως τε καὶ οἱ ἄρσενες ἀφέντες τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν τῆς θηλείας ἐξεκαύθησαν ἐν τῇ ὀρέξει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ἄρσενες ἐν ἄρσεσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην κατεργαζόμενοι καὶ τὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ἣν ἔδει τῆς πλάνης αὐτῶν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀπολαμβάνοντες.
records.gloss: Because of this handed over them the God to passions of dishonor; the both for females of them exchanged the natural use into the [use] contrary to nature, \v 27 likewise and also the males having left the natural use of the female were inflamed in the desire of them toward one another, males with males the shameless [deed] working and the recompense which was necessary of the error of them in themselves receiving.
pieces: That is why God handed them over to passions that bring dishonor. Their women gave up natural sexual use for what goes against nature.

The men did the same: they left behind natural relations with women and were set on fire with craving for one another. Males with males, they did what is shameless, and they received in themselves the fitting penalty for their straying.

L.26: Because of this God handed them over to passions of dishonor; for their females exchanged the natural use for that which is contrary to nature,
L.27: and likewise also the males, having left the natural use of the female, were inflamed in their desire toward one another, males with males committing the shameless [deed] and receiving in themselves the recompense which their error required.

R.26: That is why God handed them over to shameful desires. Their women stopped having sex in the natural way and did what is against nature.
R.27: The men did the same. They stopped having natural sex with women, and they burned with desire for one another. Men did shameless things with men. And in themselves they received the punishment their wrong deserved.

decisions.reason: Verses 26-27 belong to Paul's account of humanity turning from the Creator (1:18-32). At 2:1 he turns to the reader who judges others for these things and says that all alike need the gospel (3:9, 3:23).
χρῆσις is "use" or "function". Greek writers used it for sexual relations, and the context here makes that the sense.

decisions.choice: natural, against nature: the order the Creator made
alternatives: what is customary in a culture
decisions.reason: "Nature" here is the way God made the world (verses 20 and 25 speak of the Creator and his works). Paul can use "nature" for custom (1 Corinthians 11:14), but here it is set against the exchange of the Creator for the creature.

decisions.choice: female and male: the words of Genesis 1:27
decisions.reason: θῆλυς and ἄρσην are not the usual words for women and men but "female" and "male", the words the Greek translation of Genesis 1:27 uses: "male and female he created them". The passage looks back to the creation account, as verse 23 does.

decisions.choice: the verse does not name what the women exchanged it for
decisions.reason: Verse 26 says only that the women exchanged natural relations for what is against nature. "Likewise" at the start of verse 27 ties it to what follows, which suggests relations between women; it has also been read of other sexual acts. The translation keeps the verse's own general wording.
ἀσχημοσύνη is shamelessness, an indecent act; with the article it is the act just described.

ἀντιμισθία is a payment in return. "Their error" (literally a wandering from the way) looks back to the exchange of God for idols (verses 23, 25). Paul does not say what the penalty is; it may be the handing over itself, the lives they are left to.
"Use" alone would not be understood in English; Balanced and Readable say what it refers to.
English "females" and "males" sound clinical. Literal keeps them so the Genesis wording stays visible; Balanced says "males with males" once to keep the echo.

records.source: Καὶ καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα, πεπληρωμένους πάσῃ ἀδικίᾳ πονηρίᾳ πλεονεξίᾳ κακίᾳ, μεστοὺς φθόνου φόνου ἔριδος δόλου κακοηθείας, ψιθυριστάς, καταλάλους, θεοστυγεῖς, ὑβριστάς, ὑπερηφάνους, ἀλαζόνας, ἐφευρετὰς κακῶν, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς, ἀσυνέτους, ἀσυνθέτους, ἀστόργους, ἀνελεήμονας·
records.gloss: And as not they saw fit the God to have in knowledge, handed over them the God to unfit mind, to do the [things] not being fitting, \v 29 having been filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, malice, full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, ill will, whisperers, \v 30 slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, boasters, inventors of evil [things], to parents disobedient, \v 31 senseless, faithless, unloving, merciless;
pieces: And since they did not think God worth acknowledging, God handed them over to a worthless mind, and so they do things that should never be done.
Every kind of wrongdoing fills them: wickedness, greed, malice. They are brimming with envy, murder, rivalry, deceit and spite. They whisper about others
and speak against them; they hate God; they treat others with contempt; they are proud and full of boasting; they think up new evils; they defy their parents;
they are without sense, without loyalty, without love, without mercy.

L.28: And since they did not see fit to keep God in [their] knowledge, God handed them over to an unfit mind, to do the things that are not proper,
L.29: filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, malice, full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, ill will, gossips,
L.30: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

R.28: They did not think it was worth knowing God. So God handed them over to minds that are worth nothing, and they do things they should never do.
R.29: They are full of every kind of wrong, evil, greed and hatred. They are jealous, they murder, they fight, they lie, and they want to hurt others. They gossip about people
R.30: and say bad things about them. They hate God. They treat others with contempt. They are proud and they boast. They think up new ways to do evil. They do not obey their parents.
R.31: They are foolish. They do not keep their promises. They do not love others or show them mercy.

decisions.choice: a play on words: they did not see fit, so God gave them an unfit mind
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζω is to test and approve; ἀδόκιμος is what fails the test, worthless. They judged God not worth knowing, and God handed them over to a mind that fails every test.
ἐπίγνωσις is knowledge that recognizes and acknowledges. They knew God (verse 21) but would not keep him in their acknowledgment.
θεοστυγής was used in older Greek for those hated by the gods, but in a list of what people do it most likely means those who hate God, as the passive "hateful to God" would stand out in such a list.
ἀσύνθετος is someone who does not keep an agreement or covenant. It sounds like ἀσύνετος ("senseless") just before it, one of several sound plays in the list.

alternatives: many later manuscripts add "sexual immorality" after "unrighteousness" in verse 29
many later manuscripts add "implacable" (refusing to make peace) after "unloving" in verse 31
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts do not have these two words, and the SBLGNT leaves them out. Many later manuscripts, and the printed Greek editions of the sixteenth century, include them. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: see fit / unfit; worth / worthless; worth / worth nothing
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the play on words with a matching pair of English words.

decisions.choice: the list is grouped into clauses
alternatives: a list of nouns and adjectives
decisions.reason: A list of twenty-one words is hard to follow when read aloud. Balanced keeps every item and order but groups them into short clauses with verbs.

records.source: οἵτινες τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιγνόντες, ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες ἄξιοι θανάτου εἰσίν, οὐ μόνον αὐτὰ ποιοῦσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ συνευδοκοῦσιν τοῖς πράσσουσιν.
records.gloss: Who the righteous decree of the God having known, that the [ones] the such [things] practicing worthy of death are, not only them do but also approve the [ones] practicing.
pieces: They know God's just decree, that people who do such things deserve to die, yet they not only do them but cheer on others who do them.

L.32: Although they know the righteous decree of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, they not only do them but also approve of those who practice [them].

R.32: They know what God has said is right: people who do these things deserve to die. But they keep doing them anyway. And they are glad when others do them too.

decisions.reason: δικαίωμα is a just requirement or decision, here God's verdict on such deeds. It is from the same root as "righteousness" (verse 17).
Death here is God's judgment, as Paul says later: "the wages of sin is death" (6:23). The verse states what people deserve before God.
"Not only ... but also" makes approving others the last and worst step: they know God's verdict, and still encourage others in the same things. Chapter 2 then turns to the reader who condemns them.
συνευδοκέω is to give hearty approval; "cheer on" catches its warmth.
